# <label>: # The layer decomposition on chrI. Every row uses the SAME trainDir
# (robocop_train_fiberonly) except the EM ones, so the only variable is which emission
# layers are live -- the masks are one line each in robocopExtras.py.
# label            seq  fib   what it answers
# seq              ON   off   what does sequence alone buy? the floor fib+seq must beat
# fib              off  ON    what does Fiber-seq alone buy?
# fib+seq          ON   ON    the standard run
# fib+wide*        off  ON    does widening help the FIBER footprint, with the PWM out of
#                             the way? the sharpest test of the widening hypothesis
# NAMING (established 2026-09-04). The directory name IS the label, so what you read in the
# published viewer is what sits on disk. Punctuation is the only difference, since a path
# 'fib_seq_' means both emission layers are live; 'fib_' means Fiber-seq only, sequence
# layer masked off. The older scheme named directories after the MASK applied
# (maskoff_revfix, seq_maskoff_capA, conclo_0p01, widememe, wide10all) while labels named
# the LAYERS -- two systems that had drifted apart; they were reconciled by renaming the
# directories. Anything written before that date may use the old names.
# Assets that are NOT runs keep their own names on purpose: pkgvar/{seq,fiber}_maskoff_*
